worked.title: Q1 · Signal tower: Lagrangian and KKT (10 marks)

problem.text: Tower at (0, 0); cost = squared distance; region {7 − 2x + y ≤ 0, 0 ≤ x + y + 5}. (i) Formulate. [1.5M] (ii) Lagrangian. [0.5M] (iii) KKT conditions. [4M] (iv) Solve with KKT. [4M]

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: The full KKT route on a two-constraint problem. Marks: (i) 1.5, (ii) 0.5, (iii) 4, (iv) 4.

steps.label: Plan of attack
steps.text: 1. Objective = squared distance; constraints in g ≤ 0 form. 2. Lagrangian. 3. List the KKT conditions. 4. Express x, y through λ, put into slackness, test the four cases, keep the one with λ ≥ 0 that is feasible.

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: This paper's symbols are the board's: λ₁, λ₂ ≥ 0.

steps.label: STEP 1 · (i) Problem
steps.text: min x² + y² [0.5M] s.t. 7 − 2x + y ≤ 0 and x + y + 5 ≥ 0, i.e. −5 − x − y ≤ 0 [1M].

steps.label: STEP 7 · (iv) Case λ₁ = λ₂ = 0
steps.text: x = y = 0, but 7 − 0 + 0 = 7 > 0: infeasible ✗

steps.label: STEP 9 · (iv) Other cases
steps.text: λ₁ = 0, λ₂ > 0: 5 + λ₂ = 0 ⇒ λ₂ = −5 < 0 ✗. Both > 0: 2.5λ₁ + 0.5λ₂ = 7 and 0.5λ₁ + λ₂ = −5 ⇒ λ₁ ≈ 4.2, λ₂ ≈ −7.1 < 0 ✗ [1M for the list of cases].

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text:
• Keeping a case with a negative λ.
• Not checking the inactive constraint in the surviving case.

steps.text: [Lecture 11, Lagrangian tab](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch11/f-lagrange/12).

worked.title: Q2 · Cubic critical points, zone of attraction; Lagrange on a plane (10 marks)

problem.text: (A) f(x) = ax³ + bx² + cx + d, a > 0. (a) Condition for two distinct critical points; find them and classify. [3M] (b) The zone of attraction of each local minimum under gradient descent. [3M]  (B) min ax + by + cz s.t. px + qy + rz = 0: when is there a solution, how many, and the objective value there? [4M]

steps.label: (A)(a)
steps.text: f′ = 3ax² + 2bx + c = 0 ⇒ x₁,₂ = (−b ∓ √(b² − 3ac))/(3a); two distinct real roots iff **b² − 3ac > 0**. f″ = 6ax + 2b is negative at x₁ (maximum) and positive at x₂ (minimum) [3M].

steps.label: (A)(b)
steps.text: f′ < 0 between the roots and f′ > 0 to the right of x₂, so GD moves towards x₂ from both sides. Zone of attraction of the only minimum x₂: **x > (−b − √(b² − 3ac))/(3a)** [3M].

steps.label: (B)
steps.text: Notation (kept from the key): λ is the equality multiplier (μ on the lecture boards). L = ax + by + cz − λ(px + qy + rz) ⇒ a = λp, b = λq, c = λr. A solution exists iff (a, b, c) ∥ (p, q, r); then every point of the plane is a solution and the value is 0. Otherwise the objective is unbounded below: no solution [4M].

steps.label: More
steps.text: [Lecture 11, Lagrangian tab: Q(B)](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch11/f-lagrange/15).

worked.answer: b² − 3ac > 0; x₂ = (−b + √(b² − 3ac))/(3a) is the minimum with zone x > x₁; (B) solvable iff (a, b, c) ∥ (p, q, r), then value 0 everywhere on the plane.

worked.title: Q3 · PCA on four points; PC1 and classification (10 marks)

problem.text: (A) X has rows (6, −4), (−3, 5), (−2, 6), (7, −3). (a) Covariance matrix, its unit eigenvectors and eigenvalues. [4M] (b) Project onto one dimension: which subspace, and each point's coordinate. [3M] (c) Sketch. [1M]  (B) Is it always true that two classes projected on PC1 can be separated by a threshold? [2M]

steps.label: (b)
steps.text: Project onto span{(1, −1)}: zₙ = e₁ᵀ(xₙ − x̄) ⇒ 9/√2 ≈ 6.36, −6.36, −6.36, 6.36. PC1 keeps 40.5/41 ≈ 98.8% of the variance.

steps.label: (c)
steps.text: On the PC1 line the points fall in two pairs: (6, −4) and (7, −3) at +6.36, (−3, 5) and (−2, 6) at −6.36.

steps.label: (B)
steps.text: **No.** PC1 follows the largest variance, not the class split. Counter-example: class A at (x, +0.1) and class B at (x, −0.1) for x from −10 to 10. PC1 is the x-axis, both classes project onto the same range, and no threshold separates them, even though y = 0 does.

worked.answer: S = [[20.5, −20], [−20, 20.5]]; λ = 40.5 (1, −1)/√2 and 0.5 (1, 1)/√2; coordinates ±6.36; PC1 need not separate classes.

worked.title: Q4 · Soft-margin C; echelon form and the four subspaces (10 marks)

problem.text: (A) Noisy-sensor data, quadratic-kernel SVM with parameter C. Sketch a boundary for small C and for large C; mark a point whose wrong label would not / would affect the boundary; high or low C? [5 × 1M]  (B) f(x₁, x₂, x₃) = (2x₁ + x₂, 3x₁ + 7x₂ + 3x₃, 3x₁ + x₂ + x₃). (A) Its matrix in row echelon form. [2M] (B) Basis of the column space. [1M] (C) Basis of the null space. [1M] (D) Independent rows. [1M]

steps.label: (A)
steps.text: Small C: smooth boundary, wide margin, a few violations. Large C: tight boundary, narrow margin, few misclassifications. A non-support vector's label does not matter; a support vector's does. Noisy data ⇒ **low C** [1M each].

steps.label: (B)(B)
steps.text: Every column has a pivot ⇒ the three columns are a basis of the column space; rank 3 [1M]. (det A = 14 ≠ 0.)

steps.label: (B)(C)
steps.text: Null space = {0}; its basis is empty, dimension 0 [1M].

steps.label: (B)(D)
steps.text: All three rows are independent (rank 3) [1M].

steps.label: More
steps.text: [Lecture 15, Soft margin tab: small vs large C](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch15/f-soft/7).

worked.answer: Low C for noisy data; A has rank 3: columns are a basis, null space {0}, all rows independent.
